note: Thresholds for the three data checkpoints. Written before the first measurement on the real data and not changed afterwards (CONTRIBUTING rule 5). Published reference values are quoted from the sources named here.

checkpoint_1_checksums.rule: every file in data/manifest/manifest.json exists under the data root with the recorded size and SHA-256; every large file was also re-read from its second source and matched (cross_checks)

checkpoint_2_georeferencing.published_coordinates: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (USGS), features Shackleton 5450, Shoemaker 5494, Faustini 1919, Cabeus 953, de Gerlache 1439, Haworth 14502; stored in data/checkpoints/features.json with URL and retrieval time
checkpoint_2_georeferencing.outline_choice: for each crater the determination with the most outline vertices (at least 5)
checkpoint_2_georeferencing.method: for up to 60 evenly spaced outline vertices, search the radial line from the outline centroid, +-1500 m around the vertex in 20 m steps, on the 20 m product; the crest is the highest point on that line; offset = distance from vertex to crest

checkpoint_3_values_and_reference_radius.label_derived_min_max: measured minimum and maximum DN of each polar file equal DERIVED_MINIMUM and DERIVED_MAXIMUM in its label, exactly

shackleton_reference.source: Zuber et al. 2012, Nature 486, 378-381, Table 1 (NASA NTRS 20120013758): centre of rim 89.655 S, 129.174 E; lunar radius at floor centre 1734.63 km; mean rim height above the 1737.4 km datum 1.3 km; mean depth rim to floor 4.1 +- 0.05 km. The datum is the 1737.4 km sphere, the same as the LOLA GDR OFFSET.
shackleton_reference.rim_height_definition: mean crest height over the Shackleton outline vertices (crest search as in checkpoint 2)

overlap_20m_vs_60m.method: 60 m pixel values against the mean of the aligned 3 x 3 block of 20 m pixels, over the full 20 m extent

cylindrical_16ppd_vs_polar.method: LDEM_16 values at its pixel centres with latitude <= -80.5 degrees, against the polar 20 m product area-mean overview with pixels <= 1.9 km (bilinear), both in metres above the 1737.4 km sphere
